chapter: Highlights, the reunion album and fellow musicians
title: Playing Harlem Uptown House, Loew's State and the Paramount
summary: He compares the downtown clubs and theaters and how long each let him play.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: It's kind of hard for me to pick one highlight. I don't know cause I really enjoyed them all. You know? And what I had mentioned to you, but once I got to downtown on Broadway, oh, at the theaters. I had played Broadway like uptown, Harlem Uptown House, Harlem Uptown. That was the first club on 51st, 52nd and Broadway. Hazel Scott was the pianist. The intermission pianist there. She was about 18 or 19 years old when I played there.
And, another theater I played at was Loew's State which you could only do about 20 minutes cause they had kind of acts. You know, they did 5 or 10 minutes, but the band just did 20 minutes.
And then, when I got the chance to get to the Paramount and all that, well, we did the whole show besides what acts we had there with it. It was nice.
